transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I guess what brings me in is, after I have one of those times where I overdo it with food, I’ll sit there and see the empty containers, and I just feel… pretty ashamed. Disgusted with myself, honestly. Like I’m not the steady, in-control man I’ve always tried to be. I don’t know if that makes sense, but it’s been bothering me enough that I figured I should talk to someone.
After you overeat, do you ever try to compensate for it by making yourself sick, exercising a lot, or doing something else to try to 'undo' the food?

I don’t… I don’t think so. I mean, I feel bad afterward, sure, but I’m not making myself sick or anything like that. I wouldn’t say I do something to undo it, at least not in any organized way. Is that what you mean?
When you overeat, do you feel like you can’t stop eating or control how much you’re eating at the time?

Yeah… I mean, I’d like to say I can rein it in, and sometimes I tell myself I’m going to. But once I start, it’s like the discipline I had on the road just kind of shuts off. I’ll be thinking, Magin, put the fork down, come on, and my hand still goes back for more.

That’s… that’s not a very good answer, I know, but it’s honestly how it feels.

Can you describe what happens during one of these times when you feel like you can't control your eating — how much do you typically end up eating, and how does it compare to what others might eat in the same situation?

Well… I guess it’s more than a normal dinner, if I’m being honest. Like some evenings I’ll heat up what I tell myself is just one bowl of pozole, and then… somehow I’ve gone through the whole pot. And maybe a couple tamales too, chips, whatever leftovers are there.

It’s embarrassing to say, but it’s like I’m eating enough for a whole crew, not just me sitting there by myself. I know most people wouldn’t eat that much in one sitting.
Do these episodes of overeating bother you enough that they affect your daily life, like making you avoid social situations or causing problems at work or home?

A little, yeah… I mean, I still get my work done, mostly. I don’t want to make it sound like everything’s falling apart.

But I have started dodging some check-in calls from drivers I’m supposed to be mentoring. That’s not like me. I just feel… ashamed, I guess, and I don’t want them hearing how far off my routine I’ve gotten. I know that probably sounds silly, but it has been getting in the way some.
During these times when you feel like you're overeating, do you feel like you've lost control — like you can't stop eating even if you wanted to?

Yeah… I think that’s the part that bothers me most, honestly. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m helpless or anything, but once I start, it’s like the discipline I used to have on the road just kind of shuts off.

I’ll be sitting there telling myself, “Magin, put the fork down, that’s enough,” and then my hand still goes back for more anyway. So… yeah, I guess I do feel like I’ve lost control in those moments.
How often do you find yourself having these episodes where you feel like you’ve lost control while eating?

Um… more often than I’d like to admit, I guess. Since I’ve been home with this back injury, it’s been several nights most weeks.

I mean, I don’t think it’s every single night, but… looking back over these last three months, I can’t really think of a week where it didn’t happen at least once. Does that make sense?

When you say you eat more than a normal dinner, can you clarify — are you eating amounts that most people would clearly consider much larger than what anyone would typically eat in that same time period?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to exaggerate, but yes. Some evenings I’ll tell myself I’m just heating up one bowl of pozole, something normal, and then… somehow I’ve gone through most of the pot.

And it’s not just that. I’ll add a couple tamales, some chips, whatever leftovers are in the fridge. When I look at it afterward, it’s like I was feeding a whole crew, not just me. So… yeah, I think most people would probably say that’s a lot.
Do you find that how you see your body, or how much you weigh, has a strong impact on how you feel about yourself overall?

I’m not sure, doctor. I mean… I don’t love that I’ve put on weight, sure, and I probably complain about it more than I should. But I don’t know if I’d say it controls how I feel about myself overall.

I still try to see myself as a hardworking guy, a decent husband, you know… not just whatever the scale says. Maybe it bothers me more than I’m admitting, but I don’t want to make it sound like that’s the whole of who I am. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you feel that your weight or body shape influences how you judge yourself, like feeling that you’ve failed if you don’t meet your own expectations about how you should look?

I don’t know if I’d put it as “failed,” exactly. I mean… I definitely don’t like the way my clothes fit lately, and I’ll get disappointed in myself, sure.

But I’m trying not to make it sound bigger than it is. I don’t wake up thinking I’m worthless because of my shape or anything like that. It bothers me, yeah, but I guess I’m not totally sure how much it affects how I judge myself. Does that make sense?
Do you feel upset or distressed about your body shape or weight most of the time, not just after overeating?

I’m… not sure I’d say most of the time. I notice it, yeah — like when I’m getting dressed or if I catch myself in a mirror — and I don’t feel great about it.

But it’s not like I’m sitting there all day thinking about my weight, if that makes sense. After I overeat it’s definitely worse, but outside of that… I guess it comes and goes. I don’t want to overstate it.
Do you feel marked distress about your body shape or weight most of the time, even outside of these episodes when you overeat?

I’m not sure I’d call it “marked,” honestly. I mean, I don’t feel good about my weight, and I notice it at times, but I wouldn’t say it’s most of the time outside of when I’ve overeaten.

Maybe I’m downplaying it a little, I don’t know… but it feels more like it comes up in certain moments, not like it’s always sitting on me. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Do you ever feel like you're eating rapidly, eating until you're uncomfortably full, or eating large amounts of food when you're not physically hungry?

Yeah… I mean, sometimes I do eat pretty fast. I don’t love admitting that, but it’s like I’m still on a tight delivery schedule or something, just trying to get it down and move on.

There are times I barely taste it, and then I realize I’m kind of breathing hard because I’ve been shoveling food in without really slowing down. I know that probably sounds bad, but… yeah, that does happen.
Do you ever find yourself eating large amounts of food even when you're not physically hungry?

Yeah… I guess I do. Not every night, but some evenings I’ll tell myself I’m just going to heat up one bowl of pozole, you know, something reasonable.

And then… before I really catch up to what I’m doing, I’ve gone through most of the pot, and maybe a couple tamales, some chips, whatever leftovers are there. It’s embarrassing to say it like that — like I’m eating for a whole crew instead of just me.

I don’t always feel hungry when it starts, or not hungry enough for all that. I know that’s probably what you’re asking.
Do you often find yourself eating much more quickly than normal, eating until you feel uncomfortably full, or eating even when you're not really hungry?

Yeah… I mean, I probably should say yes to that. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but there are times I keep going past the point where I know I should stop.

Like, my stomach will feel stretched out and actually hurt, and with my back being bad, I’ll end up just stuck in the recliner afterward feeling miserable. Even getting up feels like too much at that point.

I know that’s not great. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
